_meta.title: FrancoPath Verb Conjugations — Edge Cases & Irregulars
_meta.purpose: The 35 verbs that cause 90% of French conjugation problems. Fully conjugated across all the tenses your app needs at A1-B2. For the other ~7,000 verbs, use the import script with Verbiste/french-verbs-lefff.

schema.edge_cases: what makes this verb tricky — read this first
schema.stem_changes: spelling changes by tense (for -er verbs with stem changes)

person_codes.il: 3rd singular (il / elle / on) — same form for all three

_meta.notes: For passé composé, the form shown is for masculine singular subject. With être-auxiliary verbs, agreement applies: 'elle est allée', 'ils sont allés', 'elles sont allées'. The app should compute agreement at runtime.

verbs.edge_cases: The single most irregular verb. Memorize all forms — almost no patterns help. The auxiliary for many être-verbs (aller, venir, etc.). Note past participle 'été' is masculine and invariable.

Second most irregular verb. Auxiliary for most verbs in compound tenses. Used in idioms where English uses 'to be': 'avoir faim' (to be hungry), 'avoir 25 ans' (to be 25). Subjunctive forms 'aie/aies/ait' are silent and common in errors.

Looks like a regular -er but is highly irregular. Uses être as auxiliary — past participle agrees with subject: 'elle est allée', 'ils sont allés'. Also forms the futur proche: 'Je vais manger' = I'm going to eat. Future stem 'ir-' is unique.

passe_compose.il: il est allé / elle est allée
passe_compose.ils: ils sont allés / elles sont allées

verbs.edge_cases: Top-5 most used verb. Watch the spelling 'vous faites' (NOT 'faisez'). 'nous faisons' is pronounced /fəzɔ̃/ (the 'ai' becomes /ə/). Used in countless idioms: 'faire la cuisine' (to cook), 'faire du sport' (to do sports).
Watch the spelling 'vous dites' (NOT 'disez') — only 3 verbs have this -tes ending: être (êtes), faire (faites), dire (dites). Past participle 'dit'.
Modal verb — usually followed by an infinitive. 'je peux' has an alternative inverted form 'puis-je' for questions ('Puis-je vous aider?'). Future stem 'pourr-' has double r.
Modal verb. Polite form 'je voudrais' (conditional) is used much more than 'je veux' to soften requests. Imperative is rare and usually polite: 'Veuillez patienter' = Please wait.

verbs.en: to have to, must / to owe
verbs.edge_cases: Two meanings: obligation ('je dois partir' = I have to leave) AND owing ('je te dois 10 euros' = I owe you). Past participle 'dû' (m sing) takes a circumflex to distinguish from preposition 'du'. Feminine and plural drop the accent: due, dus, dues.
verbs.participe_passe: dû (m sing) / due (f) / dus (m pl) / dues (f pl)

verbs.edge_cases: Don't confuse with 'connaître' (to know a person/place). 'Savoir' = to know information or how to do something. 'Je sais nager' = I know how to swim. Subjunctive form 'sache' is unusual.

Used for being acquainted with a person or place. Note circumflex over 'i' before 't' in 'il connaît' (1990 reform allows 'connait' without circumflex but traditional spelling keeps it). All -aître verbs follow the same pattern.

Uses être as auxiliary — past participle agrees: 'elle est venue'. 'Venir de + infinitive' = to have just done something (recent past): 'Je viens de manger' = I just ate. All compound verbs (devenir, revenir, parvenir, etc.) follow this pattern.

passe_compose.il: il est venu / elle est venue
passe_compose.ils: ils sont venus / elles sont venues

verbs.edge_cases: Future stem 'verr-' has double r. Past participle 'vu'. 'Aller voir' = to visit a person ('Je vais voir ma mère' = I'm going to see my mom). Compound verb 'prévoir' follows similar pattern but future is 'prévoirai' (regular).

Used for transportation: 'prendre le bus/train/métro' = to take the bus/train/subway. Used for food/drink: 'Je prends un café' = I'll have a coffee. All compounds (apprendre, comprendre, surprendre) follow the same pattern.
Highly versatile verb. Doubles the t in plural present forms ('nous mettons' but 'je mets'). Past participle 'mis' is short. Compound verbs (permettre, promettre, soumettre) follow the same pattern.
LOOKS like a Group 2 verb (-ir) but is Group 3 — does NOT take -iss-. 'Nous partons' (NOT 'partissons'). Other -ir verbs in this pattern: sortir, dormir, sentir, servir. Uses être: 'elle est partie'.

passe_compose.il: il est parti / elle est partie
passe_compose.ils: ils sont partis / elles sont parties

verbs.en: to go out, to take out
verbs.edge_cases: AUXILIARY DEPENDS ON MEANING: 'Je suis sorti' = I went out (intransitive, être). 'J'ai sorti la poubelle' = I took out the trash (transitive, avoir). Same pattern as partir, dormir.

passe_compose.tu: tu es sorti(e) / tu as sorti
passe_compose.il: il est sorti / il a sorti
passe_compose.nous: nous sommes sorti(e)s / nous avons sorti
passe_compose.vous: vous êtes sorti(e)(s) / vous avez sorti
passe_compose.ils: ils sont sortis / ils ont sorti

verbs.edge_cases: Same -ir pattern as partir/sortir (no -iss- in plural). 'Je dors' (not 'je dormis'). Compound past tense uses avoir: 'J'ai dormi'.
Don't confuse 'je lis' (I read) with 'je ris' (I laugh) or 'je vis' (I live). Past participle 'lu'. Compound verb 'élire' (to elect) follows similar pattern.
Adds -v- in plural forms: 'nous écrivons', 'ils écrivent'. Past participle 'écrit' has a final 't'. Compound verbs (décrire, prescrire, inscrire) all follow this pattern.
Three different stems: boi- (singular), buv- (nous/vous), boiv- (ils/elles). Past participle 'bu' is short.

SPELLING-CHANGE -er verb: keeps 'e' after the 'g' before 'a' or 'o' to preserve the soft /ʒ/ sound. So 'nous mangeons' (NOT 'mangons') and imparfait 'je mangeais' (NOT 'mangais'). All -ger verbs do this: nager, voyager, partager, changer.
verbs.stem_changes: mang- → mange- before a/o (to keep /ʒ/ sound)

verbs.edge_cases: SPELLING-CHANGE -er verb: 'c' becomes 'ç' before 'a' or 'o' to preserve the soft /s/ sound. 'nous commençons' (cedilla!). All -cer verbs: lancer, placer, prononcer, avancer.

SPELLING-CHANGE: doubles the 'l' before silent 'e' endings (when next syllable has silent e). 'j'appelle' but 'nous appelons'. Future and conditional KEEP the doubled l throughout: 'j'appellerai'. Same pattern: jeter (je jette), épeler.
verbs.stem_changes: appel- → appell- when followed by a silent -e (j'appelle, ils appellent, future j'appellerai)

verbs.edge_cases: SPELLING-CHANGE: e → è before silent e endings. 'j'achète' but 'nous achetons'. Future and conditional keep è throughout: 'j'achèterai'. Same pattern: lever, peser, mener, geler.
verbs.stem_changes: e → è in stressed syllables (j'achète, but nous achetons)

verbs.edge_cases: SPELLING-CHANGE: é → è before silent e in the present tense AND subjunctive. BUT in the future and conditional, traditional spelling kept é (je préférerai) — 1990 reform now allows è (je préfèrerai). Same pattern: espérer, répéter, célébrer.
verbs.stem_changes: é → è before silent e (in present and subjunctive)

verbs.edge_cases: SPELLING-CHANGE: -yer verbs change y → i before silent e (optional for -ayer, mandatory for -uyer/-oyer). Both 'je paie' and 'je paye' are correct. For 'essayer', 'employer', 'envoyer' → mandatory: j'essaie, j'emploie, j'envoie.
verbs.stem_changes: y → i before silent e (optional for -ayer)

verbs.edge_cases: SPELLING-CHANGE -oyer verb: y → i before silent e (mandatory). PLUS irregular future stem 'enverr-' (with double r — like 'voir' future). Renvoyer follows the same pattern.
verbs.stem_changes: y → i before silent e; future/conditional stem 'enverr-' is irregular

verbs.edge_cases: PROTOTYPE Group 2 verb. Adds -iss- in plural present and throughout imparfait. About 300 verbs follow this pattern: choisir, réussir, grossir, maigrir, agir, réfléchir, remplir, obéir.
PROTOTYPE Group 1 (-er) verb. Perfectly regular — no spelling changes. ~90% of all French verbs follow this exact pattern. Use this as the template for all regular -er verbs.

REFLEXIVE/PRONOMINAL VERB. Always uses 'se' + verb, and the 'se' changes with subject: je me, tu te, il se, nous nous, vous vous, ils se. ALWAYS uses être in compound tenses, with agreement: 'elle s'est levée', 'ils se sont levés'. ALSO has the e → è spelling change.
verbs.stem_changes: e → è in stressed syllables (je me lève)

passe_compose.il: il s'est levé / elle s'est levée
passe_compose.ils: ils se sont levés / elles se sont levées

verbs.edge_cases: Almost ALWAYS used in past tense (passé composé): 'Je suis né(e) en 1990' = I was born in 1990. Past participle 'né' agrees with subject: 'elle est née', 'ils sont nés'. Same pattern as 'connaître' but with être auxiliary.

passe_compose.il: il est né / elle est née
passe_compose.ils: ils sont nés / elles sont nées

verbs.edge_cases: Three different stems: meur- (singular), mour- (nous/vous), meur- (ils). Future 'mourrai' has DOUBLE r (rare and irregular). Past participle 'mort' has a final t. Uses être: 'elle est morte'.

passe_compose.il: il est mort / elle est morte
passe_compose.ils: ils sont morts / elles sont mortes

verbs.edge_cases: Same conjugation pattern as venir but uses avoir instead of être. Compounds: obtenir, retenir, contenir, maintenir all follow this pattern. Idiom: 'Tiens !' = 'Here!' (giving something) or 'Oh!' (surprise).
TRICKY: ends in -ir but conjugates like an -er verb in the present! 'j'ouvre' (NOT 'j'ouvris'). Past participle 'ouvert' has a final t. Same pattern: couvrir, découvrir, offrir, souffrir.
Future 'courrai' has DOUBLE r (one of the few verbs with this). Past participle 'couru'. Compounds: parcourir, accourir.
